title: DUI Lawyer SEO: How DUI Attorneys Get Found on Google | CaseAuthority
meta: DUI lawyer SEO explained for DUI and DWI attorneys: what people search after an arrest, Google Maps, the pages you need, local courts, reviews and how to track calls.
h1: DUI Lawyer SEO: How DUI Attorneys Get Found on Google
lead: Most people charged with a DUI have never needed a lawyer before. Within hours of being released, many of them pick up their phone and search Google. The DUI lawyers they find first get most of the calls. This guide explains how DUI lawyer SEO works, what people search for after an arrest, how to show up in Google Maps, which pages your website needs, and how to tell whether it is bringing you clients.
quick_answer: DUI lawyer SEO is the work of getting your firm to show up in Google when someone near you searches for help with a DUI or DWI charge. It comes down to a strong Google Business Profile so you appear in the map results, a website with a clear page for each kind of DUI case you take and each court or county you cover, the exact words your state uses (DUI, DWI, OWI or OUI), steady genuine reviews, and fast answers when people call. DUI searches are urgent, often local and often made at night, so firms that are easy to find and easy to reach tend to win the case.
takeaways: People search soon after an arrest, and license deadlines can be short. Be easy to find and easy to reach.
Many DUI searches show map results at the top. Your Google Business Profile is a big part of DUI SEO.
First DUI, license suspension, refusal and felony DUI each deserve their own clear page.
If your state says DWI or OWI, your site should too.
Pages that mention the real courts and counties you work in tend to beat generic pages.
Rankings are only useful if they turn into calls and clients.

sections.answer: It is the work of getting your firm found in Google when people near you search for help with a DUI or DWI charge.
paras: SEO stands for search engine optimization. For a DUI lawyer, it simply means making sure that when someone in your area types "DUI lawyer near me" or "DWI attorney" plus their city into Google, your firm is one of the names they see and call.

There are two main places to show up. The first is the map results, sometimes called the Map Pack, which shows three local firms with their reviews and a call button. The second is the regular list of websites below the map. DUI lawyer SEO covers both: your Google Business Profile for the map, and your website for the regular results.

It is a narrower job than general [[a:criminal-law-seo|criminal law SEO]]. DUI cases have their own searches, their own deadlines and their own worries, so the firms that treat DUI as its own focus usually do better than firms that mention it once on a general criminal defense page.

sections.h2: Why Is SEO Different for DUI Lawyers?
sections.answer: DUI searches are urgent, local, often late at night, and tied to short deadlines, so being found fast and answering fast matters more than in most practice areas.
paras: A person arrested for DUI is usually scared, embarrassed and short on time. In many states there is a short window, often a matter of days, to ask for a hearing to fight a license suspension. That deadline pushes people to search quickly, and many will call the first firm that looks capable and answers the phone.

DUI searches are also very local. People want a lawyer who knows the court where their case will be heard. Google knows this, which is why so many DUI searches show map results at the top of the page.

Finally, DUI clients are often first time clients. They do not know what a good DUI lawyer looks like. Clear answers, real reviews and a calm, simple explanation of what happens next can matter as much to them as your years of experience.

sections.h2: What Do People Search for After a DUI Arrest?
sections.answer: Mostly a charge plus a place, "near me" searches, and urgent questions about their license, jail and penalties.
paras: Knowing the searches helps you decide which pages to build and which questions to answer. In our experience, DUI searches fall into a few groups.
list: Charge plus place: "DUI lawyer [city]", "DWI attorney [county]".
Near me: "DUI attorney near me", "best DWI lawyer near me".
License worries: "DUI license suspension hearing", "how to get my license back after DUI".
First offense: "first DUI what happens", "do I need a lawyer for a first DUI".
Serious situations: "felony DUI lawyer", "DUI with injury attorney", "second DUI penalties".
Work related: "CDL DUI lawyer", "DUI for nurses" or other licensed jobs.
Cost: "how much is a DUI lawyer".

sections.h2: How Do DUI Lawyers Show Up in Google Maps?
sections.answer: Through a complete, accurate Google Business Profile, steady genuine reviews, and a website that backs up what the profile says.
paras: Your Google Business Profile is the listing that appears in the map results. For DUI searches it is often the first thing a person sees, so it deserves real attention.

Choose the most accurate main category for your firm, and add DUI and DWI services clearly in the profile. Keep your name, address and phone number exactly the same as on your website. Add real photos of your office and team, set accurate hours, and answer the phone during those hours. If you take calls at night or on weekends, say so, because many DUI arrests happen then.

Distance plays a part too. Google tends to show firms close to the person searching, which is why firms covering several cities often need a strong website and good reviews to compete beyond their own office. Our guide to [[a:local-seo-for-criminal-defense-lawyers|local SEO for criminal defense lawyers]] covers this in more detail.

sections.h2: Which Pages Should a DUI Lawyer's Website Have?
sections.answer: One clear page for each kind of DUI case you take and each main court or county you cover, plus pages that answer the most common questions.
paras: A single DUI page that tries to cover everything rarely ranks well. Google and your visitors both do better when each topic has its own page. Start with the cases you most want and build out from there.
list: A main DUI or DWI page for your primary city.
First offense DUI.
Second and third offense DUI.
License suspension and the administrative hearing.
Refusing a breath or blood test.
Felony DUI and DUI with injury.
Underage DUI.
Commercial driver (CDL) DUI.
Drug DUI, if you take these cases.
Pages for the main counties or courts you work in.
A question page covering cost, timelines and what happens at the first court date.

sections.h2: Use the Words Your State Uses: DUI, DWI, OWI or OUI
sections.answer: Match the term people in your state actually search for, and mention the other common terms naturally.
paras: Not every state calls it a DUI. Some use DWI, some use OWI or OUI, and some use more than one term for different charges. People usually search with the word they hear from police, the court or the news in their state.

If your state mainly uses DWI, your main page title and headings should say DWI. You can still mention DUI in the text, because many people use the terms loosely, but lead with the local word. The same goes for the name of the license hearing, the agency that handles it, and the names of the local courts.
This small step is one of the easiest ways to stand apart from national template websites, which often use DUI everywhere regardless of the state.

sections.h2: Why Local Court Detail Helps DUI Pages Rank
sections.answer: Pages that mention the real courts, counties and local process show Google and readers that you actually practice there.
paras: A DUI page that could be about any city in the country gives Google little reason to rank it for your city. A page that explains how DUI cases move through your county court, where the courthouse is, what happens at the first appearance there, and how the local license hearing works is far more useful to someone facing that process.

You do not need to give away strategy. Simple, accurate information about the local process is enough to show that you know the courts. Keep it up to date, because local procedures and addresses do change.
This kind of local detail is also what AI search tools tend to pick up when they summarize answers for people, so it helps you show up in more places than just the regular results.

sections.h2: How Do Reviews Affect DUI Lawyer SEO?
sections.answer: Reviews help both rankings and calls, but DUI clients value privacy, so ask kindly, make it easy and never pressure anyone.
paras: Reviews are one of the things Google looks at for map results, and they are one of the first things a worried person reads before calling. A steady flow of recent, genuine reviews usually helps on both fronts.

DUI clients can be hesitant to post a review under their own name. That is understandable. Many firms find that a simple, polite request at the end of a case, with a direct link, works best. Some clients are happy to leave a first name or initials. Never offer anything in return for a review, and never write reviews yourself.

When you reply to reviews, be careful not to confirm that the reviewer was your client or share any details of their case. A short, general thank you is usually the safest reply. Check your state bar rules on client confidentiality before replying to reviews, especially negative ones.

sections.h2: Should DUI Lawyers Run Google Ads as Well as SEO?
sections.answer: Often both. Ads can bring calls quickly while SEO builds, and SEO keeps bringing calls without paying for each click.
paras: DUI keywords can be some of the more expensive clicks in criminal law, because many firms compete for them. Ads can bring calls quickly, which can help a new firm or a firm entering a new county. But the calls stop when the spending stops.

SEO takes longer to build, but once your firm ranks well in the map and regular results, those calls keep coming without paying for each one. Many DUI firms use ads to keep the phone ringing while their SEO builds, then adjust the balance as rankings improve.
Whichever mix you use, track where each call came from so you can compare cost per signed client fairly.

sections.h2: How Long Does DUI Lawyer SEO Take to Work?
sections.answer: Usually months, not weeks. Early movement often shows within a few months, with steadier results after that.
paras: How long it takes depends on your city, how many firms you compete with, and where your website and profile start from. A firm with an older website, some reviews and a clean profile can often see movement sooner than a brand new firm.

Fixing the basics, such as your Google Business Profile, your main DUI page and your contact details, can help early on. Building out case type and court pages, earning reviews and adding helpful local content then builds results over the following months.
Be wary of anyone who promises first place for a DUI search by a set date. Nobody controls Google, and rankings move.

sections.h2: How Do You Know if DUI SEO Is Working?
sections.answer: Track calls, forms and signed DUI clients from search and maps, not just rankings or visits.
paras: Rankings are a useful sign, but they are not the goal. The goal is more people calling about DUI cases you want to take, and more of them hiring you.

Ask every new caller how they found you and write it down. Use call tracking or separate numbers where it makes sense. Look at how many calls came from Google Maps and from your website each month, and how many of those became paying clients. If your rankings rise but calls do not, the problem may be your profile, your reviews or how the phone is answered.
Answering fast matters as much as ranking. A DUI client who reaches voicemail at night will often just call the next firm on the list.

sections.answer: One page for every DUI topic, generic national content, the wrong state terms, and no way to tell which calls came from search.
paras: Most DUI firms that struggle in Google make a few of the same mistakes.
list: One DUI page trying to cover every situation.
Copy that could be about any state, with no local courts or process.
Using DUI when the state mainly says DWI or OWI.
A Google Business Profile with the wrong category, old hours or a different phone number from the website.
No plan for reviews.
Phones that go to voicemail at night and on weekends.
Judging SEO by rankings alone, without tracking signed clients.

sections.answer: Timelines and examples here are general. Results vary, and nothing here is legal or ethics advice.
paras: Any timelines or examples in this guide are general and for illustration only. They are not promises of results for your firm. Results vary by city, competition, reviews, website, intake and the work done.

Nothing here is legal, ethics or compliance advice. Rules on lawyer advertising, reviews, testimonials and client confidentiality vary by state, and DUI laws and deadlines differ from state to state. Check your state bar's rules and your local procedures before making changes to your website or marketing.

faq.a: It is the work of getting your firm to show up in Google when people near you search for a DUI or DWI lawyer. It covers your Google Business Profile for map results and your website for the regular results.

faq.q: How Do I Get My DUI Firm in the Google Map Pack?
faq.a: Keep your Google Business Profile complete and accurate, use the right main category, keep your name, address and phone the same everywhere, earn steady genuine reviews, and back it up with a strong DUI page on your website.

faq.q: Should My Website Say DUI or DWI?
faq.a: Lead with the term your state mainly uses, because that is what most local people search for. You can still mention the other terms naturally in the text.

faq.q: How Long Does SEO Take for a DUI Lawyer?
faq.a: Usually months rather than weeks. Many firms see early movement within a few months, with steadier results after that, depending on competition and where they start from.

faq.q: Is SEO or Google Ads Better for DUI Lawyers?
faq.a: Many DUI firms use both. Ads bring calls quickly but stop when spending stops. SEO takes longer but keeps bringing calls without paying for each click.

faq.q: Can I Ask DUI Clients for Reviews?
faq.a: Yes, as long as you ask kindly, never offer anything in return and follow your state bar rules. Many DUI clients value privacy, so make it easy and never pressure anyone.
